excerpt: SpotOn is a US point-of-sale and software company for restaurants and small businesses, valued at $3.6 billion in 2022. Pricing, what it does and alternatives.
content:
SpotOn makes point-of-sale (POS) systems and software for restaurants, bars and small businesses in the United States. Its restaurant platform covers ordering and payments, table layouts, menu management, online ordering, reservations, team management, reporting and AI profit analysis, and it sells handheld and countertop hardware. It also offers a separate point-of-sale package for retail and service businesses.

SpotOn raised money quickly during 2021 and 2022. TechCrunch reported a $125 million Series D led by Andreessen Horowitz in May 2021 that tripled its valuation to $1.875 billion. In September 2021 it announced a $300 million Series E led by Andreessen Horowitz at a $3.15 billion valuation and used part of it to buy Appetize, a point-of-sale provider for stadiums and other large venues. In May 2022 it raised another $300 million in a Series F led by Dragoneer Investment Group at a $3.6 billion valuation; Restaurant Business quoted Zach Hyman as co-CEO and said SpotOn had raised more than any other private restaurant technology company the year before.

SpotOn publishes its restaurant pricing. Its All-In plan costs $0 a station per month with hardware included, and makes its money from card processing (2.79% plus 20 cents for card-present payments, 3.79% plus 20 cents keyed), with processing minimums and a two-year minimum term. Higher tiers add software features for a monthly fee. Restaurants often compare it with Toast, Square and Clover.

We have not used SpotOn for this page. It brings together SpotOn's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
